title: Strip YAML comments from resource values before matching to prevent silent false negatives
context: Values with trailing comments (e.g., `name: my-config  # note`) were including the comment in their identity text, causing them to silently fail to match the same resource's uncommented name elsewhere. This produced false negatives indistinguishable from correct conservatism — the worst failure mode for a 'no match → no edge, never guess' design.
decision: Implement quote-aware comment stripping in the extraction layer (k8sManifest.ts) before value classification. The stripper preserves `#` characters inside quoted strings and template expressions (e.g., `{{ .x | default "#fff" }}` and `"my-config#not-a-comment"`), ensuring only trailing comments at the value boundary are removed.
consequences: Resources are now correctly matched regardless of whether their YAML includes trailing comments
The 'no match, no edge, never guess' philosophy now works correctly with real-world annotated YAML
Quote-aware parsing prevents accidental damage to template expressions and quoted values containing `#`
alternatives_rejected: Stripping comments at match time (indexer.ts) — wrong architectural layer, would duplicate logic across match sites
Accepting silent false negatives — violates correctness guarantees
Relaxing the 'never guess' rule to allow loose matching — defeats the conservative design principle
